---
title: "TS 1 · Processes and end states"
---

`ts/build_pairs.py` builds pairs of end states for elementary point-defect
processes. In each pair, the initial and final states contain the same atoms in
the same order and differ only in where the moving atoms sit. The
`event_atoms` field records those atoms. Each process is set up on the
undeformed framework, and both end states then receive the same strain and
curvature. Every structure is periodic in all three directions, has at most 100
atoms, and has at least 12 Å of vacuum between periodic images.

## Processes

The processes cover vacancy migration and coalescence, bond rotations with and
without nearby defects, adatom migration, and recombination of adatoms with
vacancies:

| Process | Initial state | Final state | Interior images |
|---|---|---|---:|
| V1 hop | monovacancy | a neighbouring carbon atom has moved into the vacant site | 5 |
| V2 hop, V3/V4 hop | vacancy cluster of 2, 3 or 4 sites | a carbon atom next to the cluster has moved into one of its sites | 5 |
| V1+V1 coalescence | two monovacancies on second-neighbour sites | their common neighbour has moved into one of them, leaving a divacancy | 5 |
| V1 reconstruction switch | monovacancy with two of the three under-coordinated atoms pulled together | a different pair pulled together | 5 |
| SW formation | pristine lattice | one C–C bond rotated by 90° about its midpoint and the local surface normal | 7 |
| Bond rotation at V1, V2, V3/V4, SW or an adatom | the defect | a C–C bond within 3.5 Å of it rotated by 90° | 7 |
| Adatom hop | C, O or N on a bridge site, or H, F or N on a top site | the same atom on a neighbouring site of the same kind | 5 |
| Adatom hop near vacancy, C adatom hop near C adatom | as above, next to a monovacancy or a second C adatom | as above | 5 |
| Frenkel recombination | monovacancy and a C adatom on a bridge site 1.5–4.5 Å away | the adatom in the vacant site | 7 |
| Adatom capture at vacancy | monovacancy and an H, O, N or F adatom 1.5–4.5 Å away | the adatom at the vacancy: N or O above its centre, H or F bonded to an under-coordinated atom | 7 |

The adatom processes also place H, N, O and F adatoms (468 of the 2,000 pairs,
23 %), which were not meant to be part of the set. Those pairs went through the
NEB run, which had started before this was noticed. The candidate step
(`assemble.py`, setting `ts_region.elements` in `config.json`) skips every band
with an atom other than carbon, so the committee, the selection and the output
files are pure carbon.

Bond rotations at a divacancy include the 5-8-5 to 555-777 transformation when
the rotated bond is the right one. A bond rotation within 3.5 Å of a
Stone–Wales defect can rotate the Stone–Wales bond back, which is Stone–Wales
annihilation.

## Frameworks, strain and curvature

Sheets make up 75 % of the pairs, nanotubes 17 % and C60 8 %:

- Sheets: hexagonal $n \times n$ cells with $n = 4$–7 (32–98 atoms), or
  rectangular cells of 4-atom units with 48–80 atoms. These are smaller on
  average than in the first set, because the cost of an NEB grows with the
  number of atoms times the number of images. Sheets receive the strain modes of
  the first set (none, uniaxial up to +15 %, biaxial, shear, general) and are
  flat (45 %), carry a 1D ripple (35 %) or carry a 2D ripple (20 %). Ripples
  come with in-plane compression, which keeps them in place when the end states
  relax with the cell fixed. Bumps and random corrugation are not used, because
  they would flatten during the relaxation.
- Nanotubes: the nine armchair and zigzag tubes of the first set, with axial
  strain from −3 % to +12 % in 70 % of pairs and an elliptical cross-section in
  40 %.
- C60 in a 22 Å cubic cell.
